desc.en: Bio Carina de Vries Carina de Vries is a Microsoft MVP for Teams and Copilot, an IT adoption expert, and the founder of Workspace Heroes. For more than thirteen years, she has helped organizations not only implement technology, but make it understandable, usable, and valuable for the people who work with it every day. Her career started as an application manager for office automation. That background gave her a broad understanding of the digital workplace: from infrastructure and IT management to end users, work processes, and change readiness. It allows her to quickly identify where organizations get stuck when moving to cloud technology, Microsoft 365, Teams, and Copilot. Carina is often asked to support complex adoption and migration projects, especially in organizations where technology has already been rolled out, but real usage is still lagging behind. Her belief is clear: IT adoption is much more than a single training session. It is about behavior, work agreements, governance, communication, leadership, and making change easier to understand and act on. With her approach, she helps organizations move from technology to behavior. One of her guiding principles is her own 3 V’s: Verwonderen, Versimpelen, and Verankeren. This means first understanding what is really happening in the workplace, then making the change smaller and easier to grasp, and finally embedding new behavior into daily work. Alongside her work as a consultant and speaker, Carina actively shares knowledge through LinkedIn, webinars, podcasts, and community events. She spoke at Microsoft Ignite, where her session on a 90-day plan for Copilot adoption was selected as one of the Top 10 MVP Theater Sessions. She is also a board member of Dutch Women in Tech, where she helps create more visibility, connection, and opportunities for women in the IT industry. Carina is known for her practical, energetic, and accessible way of explaining technology and change. She makes IT less complicated, brings technology back to everyday work, and focuses on what it should always be about: people, value, and impact. Official Microsoft MVP profile: https://mvp.microsoft.com/en-US/MVP/profile/5b59c220-f74f-467f-aa7a-fada6f14d618

desc.en: Glen Scales is a Microsoft MVP and senior developer based on the Sunshine Coast, Australia, specializing in Exchange, Active Directory, Office 365, and Teams. If you've ever searched for an answer to an Exchange development question, chances are Glen's work pointed you in the right direction. desc.en: Greg Zelfond is the founder of SharePoint Maven, a Microsoft MVP, and an independent Microsoft SharePoint and Microsoft 365 consultant with 20+ years of experience. He works directly with small-to-midsize businesses and nonprofits to get more out of SharePoint Online and Microsoft 365 – without custom code, without third-party tools, and without the overhead of a large consulting firm. SharePoint Maven serves clients in every time zone and across six continents. All consulting and training is delivered remotely via web meetings from his home office in Boston, MA (USA). Why SharePoint Doesn’t Have to Be Hard SharePoint has a reputation for being complicated, expensive, and consultant-dependent. That reputation comes from the way most large consulting firms approach SharePoint – they sell custom development, third-party add-ons, and additional licenses, because that’s how the business model works. The result is intranets and document management systems that nobody on the client side can maintain, configurations that break when Microsoft updates SharePoint, and bills that keep growing despite the project being completed. SharePoint Maven works the opposite way: out-of-the-box only, fixed-fee, and built to be maintained by your IT and Business users.

I am a Cloud Enthusiast, Tech Lead, Microsoft Intune MVP in the category Security, as well as a Blogger and Speaker with a strong focus on endpoint security. My core expertise lies in Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, and Entra ID Protection, where I spend most of my time helping IT teams of various sized organizations strengthen their security posture in a practical, sustainable, and scalable way. In addition, I am the founder of AdVision Swiss AG a swiss-based MSP and MSSP. Alongside delivering large-scale customer projects, I also serve as the managing CEO, where my focus is on standardizing deployments with strict baselines & managed services and on scaling our teams further, building strong engineering capabilities, and continuously raising the technical bar across the organization. I place a strong emphasis on developing engineers into highly skilled, security-minded professionals who can confidently design and deliver modern cloud solutions. I enjoy working at the intersection of technology, leadership, and execution balancing hands-on technical depth with the responsibility of growing a company and its people. If you are interested in endpoint & cloud security with Entra ID, Intune and Defender feel free to connect or reach out. I am always happy to exchange ideas, discuss challenges, and share lessons learned from real-world implementations. desc.en: Dominiek Verham is a Principal Consultant at Open Line, where he helps organizations to enhance their desktop experience and transition to modern workplace solutions. His work focusses on designing and implementing technologies across modern workplace, desktop environments, Azure infrastructure and Microsoft security platforms. He has a strong interest in new technologies and actively collaborates with partners while sharing his knowledge with the community through his personal blog and contributions to the Windows 365 community. Dominiek served as a technical reviewer for both the first and second editions of Mastering Windows 365, written by Christiaan Brinkhoff, Sandeep Patnaik and Morten Pedholt. This experience gave him valuable insight into the publishing process and ultimately led him to co-author his own book with his good friend Johan Vanneuville. In June 2024, he co-authored Securing Cloud PCs and Azure Virtual Desktop, a practical guide that explores Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop and related Azure solutions in-depth. The book covers use cases, decision-making considerations between the two solutions, and best practices for securing both new and existing environments. He regularly participates in community events, where he enjoys connecting with peers and delivering sessions on topics such as Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop, Microsoft Intune, Nerdio and EUC solutions. Since 2022, Dominiek has been recognized as a Microsoft MVP and Nerdio NVP, acknowledgements he considers a great honor. His certifications include Microsoft 365 Enterprise Administrator Expert, Microsoft Certifified Azure Solutions Architect Expert, and Azure Virtual Desktop specialty. Dominiek values community engagement and welcomes opportunities to connect, whether through social media or community events. Official Microsoft MVP profile: https://mvp.microsoft.com/en-us/PublicProfile/5004915?fullName=Dominiek+Verham

desc.en: Enterprise data estates are where AI ambitions go to die. The board wants Copilot, RAG, and agentic workflows. The estate can't carry any of it, fragmented governance, legacy pipelines, no semantic layer, and a "data strategy" that's really just a migration backlog. That's the gap where AI projects stall, budgets spiral, and leadership loses confidence in the entire programme. I founded Onyx Data to close that gap. Over 15 years we've built a practice of Microsoft-certified consultants and the Onyx Impact Framework, a governance-first methodology that defines outcomes before pipelines, builds semantic models before dashboards, and measures ROI like a product, not a project. Across global enterprise engagements it has delivered £93M in revenue growth, including an Elcome International and SpaceX deployment that went from concept to production in six weeks, recognised by Microsoft as a customer success story at Build and Ignite. Then we built FabOps an AI-powered governance platform for Microsoft Fabric, on Azure Marketplace and Microsoft Co-Sell Ready. It's the control tower for Fabric estates: real-time governance scoring across eight dimensions, cost attribution, performance monitoring, and AI-powered recommendations that keep the estate governed as it scales. The path is a ladder every step on Azure Marketplace: • Strategy & Enablement — align your leadership team. • 4-Week Fabric Accelerator — your first governed production workload, live. • FabOps — keep it governed, continuously. Every pilot that stalls before production has a price. I call it the Pilot Tax, and the fastest way to stop paying it is the Pilot Tax Assessment: a fixed-scope, two-week diagnostic that maps your path from stalled pilots to governed production. Start here: https://onyxdata.co.uk/pilot-tax-assessment I also write The Pilot Tax, the newsletter on making AI ROI visible at board level: thepilottax.substack.com 5× Microsoft MVP · Oxford Saïd AI Programme alumnus · Forbes Technology Council member · Author of the LinkedIn Learning course, How to Build a Successful Data Strategy · Writing The Soul of the Machine: Nine Principles of AI Stewardship. Official Microsoft MVP profile: https://mvp.microsoft.com/pt-br/mvp/Leon%20Gordon-5004342

desc.en: Patrick Wahlmueller is a Microsoft MVP, IT professional, speaker, and community organizer from Austria with more than a decade of experience in IT automation and Microsoft technologies. Today, his main focus is on Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, GitHub Copilot, AI agents, and the practical governance of enterprise AI. desc.en: Asif Rehmani helps organizations turn Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses into daily habits. He is the founder and CEO of VisualSP, a Microsoft-native digital adoption platform, and a 20-time Microsoft MVP, now recognized for Microsoft Copilot. He has trained people on Microsoft technologies since 2002, has spoken at conferences since 2007 in the US, Europe, Canada and New Zealand, and is the author of four books on technology adoption. His work focuses on what happens after the licenses are bought: helping users know what to ask Copilot, measuring whether it is working, and keeping usage from stalling after launch.
